contract.explicit_requirement: No explicit contract constraint found for searchParams.nprobe, but contract has milvus_range_indexes_create_001 requiring nlist >= 1 for index creation, establishing precedent for IVF parameter validation

physical.objective_constraint: For IVF (Inverted File) indexes, nprobe represents the number of inverted lists to probe during search. Physical constraint: nprobe must be >= 1 (probing 0 lists makes search meaningless) AND nprobe <= nlist (cannot probe more lists than exist). nprobe=0 violates the lower bound.

perspective_analysis.aggregation_applied: verdict_B=CONFIRMED (physical violation) AND verdict_C=CONFIRMED (not graceful) -> final=CONFIRMED

verdicts.rationale: API accepts nprobe=0 and nprobe=-1 without error, returning HTTP 200 with valid search results. Source code analysis of generateSearchParams() (utils.go:2076-2131) shows NO validation of nprobe range - parameters are simply converted to strings using fmt.Sprintf(). Physical constraints require nprobe >= 1 for IVF indexes (probing 0 lists is meaningless). This matches developer_cognition blindspot 'REST v2 API data type serialization'. Unlike the nlist parameter which has explicit validation (milvus_range_indexes_create_001), nprobe lacks any range checking in the REST v2 layer.
